key_insight: A parameter-free, ab initio Green–Kubo framework can predict charge transport in molecular semiconductors directly from electron–phonon Hamiltonians, revealing transport regimes and bottlenecks without assuming a specific mechanism.
engineering_relevance: This enables more reliable screening and design of organic semiconductor materials for transistors and photovoltaics by linking atomic structure to mobility, temperature dependence, and conductivity.
method: Compute electron–phonon interactions from first principles across the full phonon spectrum.
Propagate carriers on hundreds-of-molecule domains using nonperturbative Green–Kubo dynamics.
Extract mobility, temperature exponents, and optical-conductivity signatures from emergent transport behavior.
evidence_signal: The framework was validated across five representative crystals, reproducing measured mobilities, temperature exponents, and optical-conductivity fingerprints.
watch_item: The approach is computationally demanding and requires high-quality ab initio electron–phonon Hamiltonians, which may limit routine large-scale screening.
paper_title: First-Principles Origins of Charge Transport in Molecular Semiconductors
